subject.title: [Feature]: Discord self-profile updates (strict bot-only scope for nickname/avatar/status)

question: Should OpenClaw add a Discord plugin-owned `self-profile` action/API for bot-only nickname, avatar, status, and activity updates, and what gate, account-selection, validation, audit, and partial-failure contract should it use?
rationale: The current code lacks the requested surface, and implementing it would create a new public config/API plus a bot-credential-backed identity mutation path that automation should not choose without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Approve narrow self-profile action
options.body: Add a Discord-owned, default-off `self-profile` action with strict self-only checks, explicit multi-account routing, avatar validation, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Limit to presence controls
options.body: Reject nickname/avatar mutation for now and route only status/activity needs through the existing presence action or the separate plugin-runtime presence API discussion.

options.title: Defer identity mutation
options.body: Keep bot identity changes manual or external until maintainers define a broader Discord identity model across self-profile, per-binding identity, and webhook persona delivery.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow self-profile action
recommendation.body: Add a Discord-owned, default-off `self-profile` action with strict self-only checks, explicit multi-account routing, avatar validation, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest merged Discord presence-health work and that PR explicitly scoped out self-profile behavior.
